Grill-me asks one question at a time
claim: The grill-me skill instructs the agent to interview the user relentlessly about every aspect of a plan, walk the design tree, resolve dependencies one-by-one, provide a recommended answer, ask questions one at a time, and explore the codebase instead when a question can be answered from code.
evidence: Skill text: 'Ask the questions one at a time' and 'If a question can be answered by exploring the codebase, explore the codebase instead.'
relevance: Defines the interview loop's conversational behavior and code-first default.

title: Superpowers refines ideas before coding
claim: Superpowers describes a workflow where the agent steps back before writing code, asks what the user is really trying to do, teases a spec out of conversation, shows it in digestible chunks, then proceeds to design approval, planning, and implementation.
evidence: README 'How it works' and 'Basic Workflow' sections describe brainstorming before writing code and spec/design approval before planning.
relevance: Supports adding an explicit interview/spec-refinement phase between proposal and downstream planning.

title: Cartographer separates proposal, requirements, design
claim: ADR-0007 accepts a workflow where proposals stay lightweight while core user workflow or comparable-risk changes add topic-local requirements deltas and graph-backed design artifacts before planning.
evidence: ADR-0007 Decision and Consequences sections describe proposal → requirements/design → plan separation and scope gating.
relevance: Constrains the new interview phase to bridge proposal into requirements/design without putting design details back into proposal.md.

title: Pi TUI can render custom interactive components and images
claim: Pi extensions/custom tools can render custom TUI components via ctx.ui.custom()/pi.ui.custom(), and the TUI includes an Image component for supported terminals.
evidence: Pi TUI docs document custom components via ctx.ui.custom and an Image component that renders base64 images in Kitty, iTerm2, Ghostty, and WezTerm.
relevance: Makes TUI-based interview questions and mockup screenshot display viable.

title: Project already includes Playwright browser validation stack
claim: The project package manifest includes Playwright and @vitest/browser-playwright dev dependencies plus browser test scripts.
evidence: package.json lists playwright, @vitest/browser-playwright, test:browser, and dashboard:check scripts.
relevance: A headless screenshot or browser-based mockup preview could reuse existing project tooling rather than introduce a new browser automation stack.
